solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Report on small issue of litter engulfing green (7)

indicatorNotes.engulfing: RUNT swallows ECO, holding it inside

blocks.note: the runt is the smallest of a litter of puppies or piglets

annotation.surface: Someone files a report on the weakest pup in a litter and how green it is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Green' tempts as a colour or as inexperience; it is the environmental sense, shortened to the prefix eco-.
annotation.definitionFit: Recount is a plain synonym in its storytelling sense: you recount events when you narrate them, not only when you count votes again.

entries.clue: Sanction absent leader of government, please (6)

indicatorNotes.absent leader of: the first letter of 'government' (G) is missing from the word for please

blocks.note: GRATIFY without G, the leader of Government

annotation.surface: A plea to impose a sanction now that the head of government is away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sanction' looks like a penalty here, but it is the verb: to approve formally.
annotation.definitionFit: To sanction a treaty is to ratify it, giving it formal approval.

entries.clue: Brief doubt quelled by racket gold winner (9)

indicatorNotes.Brief: cut short: QUERY loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.quelled by: held down inside, so QUER sits within the racket and gold

blocks.note: a con is a racket, a swindle

annotation.surface: A tennis player wins gold, briefly doubted but prevailing through their racket.
annotation.walkthrough: The sporting surface makes 'racket' a tennis bat and 'gold' a medal; really 'racket' is a swindle, and gold is the heraldic word, split apart by the doubt.
annotation.definitionFit: A conqueror is one who wins, a victor.

entries.clue: Just winning tackle before start of half time (7)

indicatorNotes.start of: take only the first letter of 'half'

annotation.surface: A football report: a side just ahead makes a tackle right before half-time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just' reads as 'barely' in the match report; it is the adjective meaning fair and honest.
annotation.definitionFit: An upright person is just: honest and principled.

entries.clue: Zoom call having to suppress extremes of noise (9)

indicatorNotes.suppress: TO pushes out NE and takes its place

blocks.note: first and last letters of NoisE, which are dropped
used as is, taking the place of NE

annotation.surface: Someone on a Zoom call has to mute the background racket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Zoom call' is one video-meeting phrase in the surface, but the words part: 'Zoom' alone is the definition, a zoom lens being a telephoto one.
annotation.definitionFit: A telephoto is a lens for magnifying distant subjects, what a camera zoom does.

entries.clue: Sweet and sour chops left by sink (7)

indicatorNotes.chops: cuts away the L from GLUM

blocks.note: GLUM (sour, sullen) with L for left cut out

annotation.surface: Sweet and sour pork chops left by the kitchen sink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet and sour chops' reads as a Chinese takeaway dish; 'Sweet' stands alone as the definition and 'chops' is a cutting instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A gumdrop is a chewy sweet, a small jelly candy.

entries.clue: Flourish of whirling cloth skirts (2,3)

indicatorNotes.whirling: something whirling spins round, so the cloth is turned to face the other way
indicatorNotes.skirts: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so GAR goes round the outside of OF

annotation.surface: A dancer's flourish as her cloth skirts whirl about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Skirts' looks like a noun, part of the dancer's costume, but it is a verb: goes around.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone tipped to go far is expected to do well in life, which is to flourish.

entries.clue: Old lady bearing sound of fraternity (7)

annotation.surface: An elderly woman with the bearing of a member of a fraternity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' tempts as posture; it just joins MA to SONIC, as in 'carrying'. The Freemasons are a fraternity.
annotation.definitionFit: Masonic means of the Freemasons, a secretive brotherhood or fraternity.

entries.clue: Red Mexican river bird passing over tip of Yucatán (5)

blocks.note: río is Spanish for river, as in the Rio Grande

blocks.clueFragment: bird passing over tip of Yucatán
blocks.note: JAY with Y, the tip of Yucatán, left out

annotation.surface: A red-coloured bird flies over a Mexican river near the Yucatán.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Red Mexican' pulls towards a colour or a Mexican thing; 'Red' is the wine, and Rioja is Spanish, not Mexican.
annotation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish wine, most famously red.

entries.clue: Church and religion brought up after raising of shot glasses (5-3)

indicatorNotes.brought up: in a down clue, ZEN is written upwards to NEZ
indicatorNotes.raising of: NIP lifted, reading upwards as PIN

annotation.surface: Churchgoers and the religious raise shot glasses in a toast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot glasses' is one drinking-vessel phrase in the surface; the words part, with 'shot' as NIP and 'glasses' as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Pince-nez are glasses clipped to the nose without earpieces.

entries.clue: Smitten orc left exposed in shower of pitch (5,4)

indicatorNotes.exposed in: the answer lies bare inside the run of letters that follows

annotation.surface: A lovestruck orc is left standing out in a rain shower on the pitch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shower' is not rain but 'one who shows': a clef shows the pitch of the notes on a stave.
annotation.definitionFit: A tenor clef is a musical sign fixing the pitch of the lines on a stave.

entries.clue: Cut small outgrowth of nuts (5)

blocks.note: nut is slang for head, and a horn grows out of one

annotation.surface: Someone trims a small growth on some nuts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' means heads, not something to eat.
annotation.definitionFit: Shorn is the past participle of shear, so it means cut.

entries.clue: Cast divide revolutionary new parts (5)

indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution is a turn right round, so the divide is written backwards
indicatorNotes.parts: to part something is to split it, so N splits FLUG, going into the middle

annotation.surface: A cast of actors split into parts by a revolutionary new play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors in a play, and 'parts' their roles; here 'cast' means thrown.
annotation.definitionFit: Cast and flung are both past tense of throwing.

entries.clue: Family let out a boy serving sandwiches (9)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: PAGE is the bread either side of RENT A

blocks.note: a page is a boy servant
to rent out = to let out

annotation.surface: A family rents out a boy to serve sandwiches.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Serving sandwiches' reads as a catering job; 'serving' belongs with 'boy', a page being a young servant, and 'sandwiches' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the lineage sense: your parentage is the family you come from.

entries.clue: Mobile reception bar on TV rose for biographical show (13)

indicatorNotes.Mobile: the letters move into a new order
indicatorNotes.bar: except: leave ON out of RECEPTION

blocks.note: used as is in the fodder

annotation.surface: Mobile phone signal is poor except on the TV set, which just improved for a documentary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reception bar' reads as signal strength on a phone; 'bar' means except, dropping ON.
annotation.definitionFit: A retrospective is an exhibition or programme surveying a person's life's work.

entries.clue: Expert projections about conclusion of suffering? (9)

annotation.definition: Expert projections about conclusion of suffering?

indicatorNotes.about: about in its sense of around: PRO and NOSES stand on either side of G

annotation.surface: Doctors forecast how a patient's illness will end.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a prognosis is a doctor's projection of how a disease will turn out.
annotation.definitionFit: Prognoses are medical forecasts of how an illness will end.

entries.clue: Common boundary is in fact strewn with trees cut on either side (9)

indicatorNotes.strewn: scattered, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.cut on either side: TREES loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: used as is in the fodder

annotation.surface: A shared boundary line is actually littered with felled trees.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture is a real hedge or treeline between two properties; 'cut' fits the fallen trees but trims the word.
annotation.definitionFit: An interface is the common boundary where two things meet.

entries.clue: Drive away with traffic tickets and string of penalties (5-3)

blocks.note: to tout tickets is to resell them at a mark-up; a tout is a ticket scalper

annotation.surface: A motorist speeds off with a pile of traffic tickets and fines.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Traffic tickets' reads as parking fines; 'traffic' is a verb. A penalty shoot-out settles a drawn football match with a series of penalty kicks.
annotation.definitionFit: A shoot-out decides a drawn football match by a series of penalty kicks.

entries.clue: Eg, I help to sort snakes (13)

annotation.definition: Eg, I help to sort snakes

indicatorNotes.snakes: winds about, so the letters twist into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone describes their job: helping to sort out snakes.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay; 'snakes' looks like the reptiles, but as a verb it stirs the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A herpetologist studies reptiles, so sorting snakes is their line of work.

entries.clue: Pay for current foreign-based stocks with euros (7)

indicatorNotes.stocks: keeps in stock, holding I inside

blocks.note: I is the physics symbol for current

annotation.surface: An investor buys foreign-listed shares with euros.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stocks' reads as shares in the finance surface; it is a verb, holding in stock, so the expat keeps the current inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A moral sense of paying: to expiate a crime is to pay for it by atoning or making amends.

entries.clue: Settle hours before long cases (7)

indicatorNotes.cases: to case something is to enclose it, as a box does, so IN A BIT wraps around the H

annotation.surface: Someone settles up, having been working for hours on long legal cases.
annotation.walkthrough: The trap is reading 'long' alone; the phrase 'before long' gives IN A BIT, and 'cases' is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To settle a region is to inhabit it, to make one's home there.

entries.clue: Muck carried by spades for one turning over soil (6)

indicatorNotes.carried by: what is carried is held, so the soil sits inside S and GE
indicatorNotes.turning over: turned over, EG ends up facing the other way as GE

annotation.surface: A gardener's spade carries muck as it turns the soil.
annotation.walkthrough: The gardening picture makes spades digging tools; here spades is the card suit, abbreviated S.
annotation.definitionFit: A smudge is a dirty mark, a smear of muck.

entries.clue: Well bores set up on windy bluff (9)

indicatorNotes.windy: twisting, so SET UP ON is rearranged

annotation.surface: Well-drilling rigs are erected on a windswept cliff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Well bores' reads as drilling and 'bluff' as a headland, but bluff here is the adjective: blunt and frank.
annotation.definitionFit: A bluff person is blunt and frank, which is to say outspoken.

entries.clue: Drain last of ale from hammered pewter mug (5)

indicatorNotes.Drain: empty out: take the E out of PEWTER
indicatorNotes.hammered: beaten out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: PEWTER with one E drained out

annotation.surface: Drink up the dregs of your ale from a beaten pewter tankard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pewter mug' is a tankard in the pub picture; 'mug' alone is the definition, a gullible fool.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang synonyms: a mug is a gullible fool, and a twerp a silly, contemptible one.

entries.clue: Acclaim bit of land this country’s given up (5)

indicatorNotes.given up: in a down clue, SOD UK is written upwards

blocks.note: a sod is a piece of turf
for a British setter, this country is the UK; the ’s stands for 'has'

annotation.surface: Praise for a nation that has surrendered a piece of its territory.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about ceding land; 'given up' is turning the letters upwards in this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: kudos, from the Greek for glory, is the credit and praise an achievement earns.

entries.clue: Amateur guards respecting women-only space (5)

blocks.note: a ham is an amateur, as in ham radio or ham actor

annotation.surface: Volunteer security guards keeping watch over a women-only area.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about untrained guards; a harem was the secluded women's quarters of a household.
annotation.definitionFit: A harem is the part of a household reserved for women.

entries.clue: English dons returned, unopened, a Marx work (5)

indicatorNotes.dons: puts on, so the reversed name wraps around E
indicatorNotes.returned: ARPO goes back to front as OPRA

blocks.note: Harpo, one of the Marx Brothers, without his H

annotation.surface: English academics send back an unopened copy of a book by Karl Marx.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dons' look like Oxbridge lecturers, and 'a Marx work' like Das Kapital; 'a Marx' is Harpo, of the Marx Brothers, and 'work' alone is the definition, opera being Latin for works.
annotation.definitionFit: An opera is a musical work; A Night at the Opera is also a Marx Brothers film.

entries.clue: Console dull, love-filled husband unhappy on retirement (9)

indicatorNotes.on retirement: going back, so the whole string is reversed

annotation.surface: Comfort a dull husband, once full of love, now miserable in retirement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Console' reads as the verb to comfort; it is the noun, a car's instrument panel. Love is O, from a zero score in tennis.
annotation.definitionFit: A car's dashboard is its console of instruments and controls.

entries.clue: Half undressed, shy about large exercise clothes (7)

indicatorNotes.clothes: PE dresses L, holding it inside

blocks.note: PE (physical education) around L for large

annotation.surface: A shy person half-undressed, fussing over large gym clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shy' is the verb to throw, not bashful; and 'exercise clothes' is not gym kit but PE clothing L.
annotation.definitionFit: Topless means naked above the waist, half undressed.

entries.clue: Exhausted state cops remaining in expression of defiance (2,5)

indicatorNotes.Exhausted: emptied, leaving only the outer letters of 'state'

blocks.note: the other ones = the remaining ones

annotation.surface: Tired police officers stay put in a show of defiance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cops' looks like police in the surface; it is a verb, to catch or hold.
annotation.definitionFit: 'So there!' is said to back up a point defiantly.
